cases.name: Rachael Renee “Rae Rae” Kerr
cases.about: Her obituary said, "Affectionately known as “Rae Rae” by her closest family and friends, she was raised in St. Petersburg, Florida. She attended Northeast High School and was homeschooled during her senior year, graduating in 2000. A few years later, Rachael discovered her passion for healthcare and began her studies at Galen School of Nursing, where she proudly earned her LPN certification. Rachael worked for many years as an LPN, but her true calling was in health and wellness. She fulfilled this passion by opening Loaded T in Orange Park, Florida, where she helped others live balanced, healthy lives. The community she fostered with Herbalife was a very important part of her life that she cherished. More than anything, Rachael adored her role as a mother. She treasured her children, Cameron, Raelan, and Brody, and embraced each day to the fullest alongside them. Rachael was a woman of deep faith, relying daily on her Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. She found great joy in attending Unity Baptist Church in Lake Butler, where she was a longtime and devoted member. Known also for her competitive spirit, Rachael loved playing Yellow Car, Pinochle, and Canasta; games with her family she often times dominated. Her laughter, determination, and loving heart will be remembered always by those who knew her. Her family takes comfort in knowing that Rachael had found her life partner, her peace, her soulmate in Steve Moore. Someone who loved her just as deeply as she loved."
cases.narrative:
Police found her in the yard with a gunshot wound to the neck. 

He broke into her home and took the couple’s two children into a vehicle outside. He also attempted to put Racheal into the vehicle, before she was able to escape with injuries.

After she fled, the sheriff says that Loyd took the children outside and asked them if they wanted to ‘go to heaven with dad’. He pointed the gun at each, and they both said no. He then pointed the gun at himself and fired. The children then ran to a neighbor’s house.
